title: He Kept Fighting WWII for 29 Years 🪖 #shorts
cast: a determined thin Japanese soldier with a cap, worn olive uniform patched many times, and a rifle

lines.say: This soldier kept fighting World War Two for twenty nine years after it ended.
shots: {hero} crouching in thick green jungle, rain dripping, eyes alert
close-up of {hero} with a determined face, jungle leaves around

lines.say: In 1944, Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang Island in the Philippines, with orders never to surrender.
shots: a small tropical island seen from above, deep blue sea, 1940s
an officer handing {hero} folded orders in a jungle camp

lines.say: The war ended in 1945. But Onoda believed the news was a trick.
shots: leaflets falling from a plane over the jungle
{hero} reading a leaflet and shaking his head suspiciously

lines.say: Year after year he hid in the jungle, fixing his uniform and keeping his rifle working.
shots: {hero} sewing his uniform by a tiny campfire at night
{hero} cleaning his rifle under a banana leaf shelter during rain

lines.say: Search teams, leaflets, even letters from his family could not convince him.
shots: a search party with megaphones walking through the jungle
{hero} hiding behind a tree watching the search party

lines.say: In 1974, a young Japanese traveller named Norio Suzuki found him, and became his friend.
shots: a young backpacker with a sleeping bag meeting {hero} in a jungle clearing
the two men sitting by a campfire talking, starry night

lines.say: Onoda said he would only stop if his commander ordered it. So his old commander flew to the island, and did.
shots: an old man in a suit reading a paper order aloud in the jungle

lines.say: Loyal, or just stubborn? Either way, history remembers that
shots: {hero} handing over his old sword, sunset over the island
{hero} walking out of the jungle into sunlight

description:
True story: Hiroo Onoda kept fighting World War Two in the Philippine jungle until 1974.

Loyal or stubborn? Tell us in the comments.

Japanese officer Hiroo Onoda held out on Lubang Island in the Philippines until 1974, refusing to believe WWII had ended, until his former commander came to relieve him. A true story.

Sources: Britannica; Wikipedia: Hiroo Onoda.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
